objective: Test whether immutable persistent tile versions with shared checkpoint roots can provide a useful bounded APNG random-access support envelope after retained full-canvas checkpoints failed the reference policy.

rootRepresentation.sharing: unchanged immutable tile versions are shared across checkpoint roots

layoutFamilies: fixed intervals from one through the maximum replay bound
access-weight-optimal layouts for a bounded checkpoint-count candidate set

sparseMotion.purpose: avoid assuming every one-pixel sparse update remains in the same tile

candidateSuccessCriteria: retained state is no larger than the selected retained-byte budget
worst replay is no larger than the selected replay bound
exact-pixel and disposal semantics remain delegated to the owned straight-alpha reference contract
modeled peak including one materialized output canvas is reported separately from retained feasibility
modelBoundary: Every tile touched by a frame is conservatively treated as a new immutable full-tile version even when only part of the tile changes.
A previous-disposal frame creates transient output tile versions but restores the pre-frame root; those output versions are not retained by later checkpoints.
A background clear returns a fully covered tile to the implicit transparent tile and creates a new version for a partially cleared tile.
Each retained checkpoint root is conservatively charged as a flat table containing one eight-byte reference per canvas tile plus a fixed header; unchanged tile bytes are shared across roots.

Candidate layouts are deterministic fixed-interval and access-optimal families, not a proof of global memory/replay optimality. A failed candidate case does not prove that every possible tile layout is impossible.

The model reports a conservative peak upper bound containing retained state, one full materialized output, all tiles touched by the largest frame, and root-build scratch. It does not estimate allocator fragmentation, compressed-source decode workspace, CPU, energy, thermal behavior, or physical-device pressure.
The SpecTesting separate-default previous fixture remains a future owned-decoder geometry stress case and does not activate current ImageCraft support for multi-frame separate-default APNG.
A feasible candidate is implementation evidence only, not a production or performance claim.
